history.title: The Lotus-Eaters
history.part: Energy re-shoots (odyssey/writers-room/BIBLE.md section 6): the stillest film of the Odyssey
history.hypothesis: The lotus's bliss was played as stillness (HOLDs with still: true), which on film is a frozen frame; lethargy reads as drugged if it moves like sleep: a slow sway on each body's own clock, the head nodding down and coming up late, the hand drifting out to the flowers and coming back short. The Lotus-eaters have it from the first drawing (they live on it), each scout from the moment it takes him.
history.variable: The lethargy: DROWSE (a new kind, tools/perform/intents-more.js) on the two Lotus-eaters from 0.3 s and on the three scouts after the taste (scout 1 until Odysseus seizes him, the others to the end), on its own layer ('drowse') laid over the published sheet; nothing else in the sheet recompiled.
held: the voice cut and the captions (the dead holds of the voice could not be trimmed without re-cutting the recording; not this take's variable)
every other channel of the published sheet odyssey/score/OD-B09-S03.choreo.json

history.result: Kept, with half the problem solved. Where the drug has the scouts (shot 4, the close on a scout who will not go home) the frozen frame is gone: still 0.86 -> 0.01, he sways and nods with his hands at his head; the film's still share 0.45 -> 0.30. Not solved: the opening insert and the landing wide (0-18.4 s, still 0.58 and 0.74) barely change, because the Lotus-eaters' drowse is small at that distance and the scouts are wary, not drugged, before the lotus; those 18 s are the voice's (two narrations) and could not be trimmed without re-cutting the recording, which was held. Next variable: the opening's framing (the Lotus-eaters close, at the flowers) or the cut.
